pr_title: scheduler_perf: refactor to allow arbitrary workloads
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/sig scheduling
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Currently the Kubernetes scheduler integration benchmarks support workloads of a particular kind -- simulated nodes are created and then an initial set of pods are scheduled. Once this setup is complete, a second and final set of pods are scheduled and various metrics are measured. I propose improving this to support arbitrary workloads that can support benchmarking heterogeneous mixture of pods, complex scheduling patterns, synchronisation primitives and cluster autoscaling.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93117

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

Work in progress, yet to migrate all existing tests over to the new pattern.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IxBgOUBTBSMSsX381ASdKuTiZE508YNXa5eVFRMzABk/edit?usp=sharing

issue_context.title: scheduler: support arbitrary workloads in integration benchmarks
issue_context.body:
Currently the Kubernetes scheduler integration benchmarks support workloads of a particular kind -- simulated nodes are created and then an initial set of pods are scheduled. Once this setup is complete, a second and final set of pods are scheduled and various metrics are measured. I propose improving this to support arbitrary workloads that can support benchmarking heterogeneous mixture of pods, complex scheduling patterns, synchronisation primitives and cluster autoscaling.

Please see this doc for details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IxBgOUBTBSMSsX381ASdKuTiZE508YNXa5eVFRMzABk/edit?usp=sharing

/sig scheduling
/kind feature
/cc @alculquicondor @ahg-g @Huang-Wei @ingvagabund
comments: @adtac scheduler perf generates various percentiles which we can see and observe their changes over time. In case any of the percentiles unexpectedly rises or falls down multiple times in a row, it can be seen as something wrong/good happening in the code. With the improvements you suggest, can you ensure the percentiles will still be around the same values no matter how many times you run the new suites over the same commit? Too much randomness might turn the percentiles too much unstable.
That would be about making the cases deterministic, which they should be, according to the proposed API. Don't you think?

Two things:

1. One of the soft goals I have when working on this is to also submit a diff of the benchmark percentiles reports (old vs new) to show that the percentiles haven't changed much. Functionally, the old tests should be no different from the new ones, but I can't guarantee that the percentiles would be close enough to the old values until I run the benchmarks. From the first few workloads that I've ported over, the new percentiles seem to be pretty close to the old ones.

2. Stability in the new benchmarks over multiple runs is definitely something I hope to have, agreed. At the very least, 50th percentile values should remain stable. And yes, the tests are deterministic, so test environment fluctuations notwithstanding, medians *should* look similar. 95th and 99th percentiles may have some noise, however. I haven't tested the benchmarks over multiple runs yet.

/assign

I've updated the doc to make the syntax a bit more concise whilst keeping the same functionality, PTAL (fairly minor change). This should reduce config toil a lot. Writing the same workload in the new yaml format will require fewer lines in most cases.
@adtac thanks for that, can't wait to see it in work :)

review_comments:
I just noticed that this was getting removed.

What if we make `testParams` just a dictionary?  Then each quantity (like `createPodsOp.CreatePods`) is a string, that could be one of the variables, or a plain number (I would just have 2 fields, each for one purpose).

do you mean something like this?

```
SchedulingBasic:
  500Nodes:
  - CreateNodes: 500
  - CreatePods: 500
```

This wouldn't allow us to have testCase level params (like featureGates, metricsCollectorConfig). Or do you mean to say we should keep the `workloads` field, but within that use maps? I don't mind either, but I like the ordered way of describing things with arrays. With a map, the 5000Nodes case could run before the 500Nodes case; that's probably not an issue, but it feels slightly less intuitive.
What would simpleTestCase.Params and createPodsOp.CreatePodsParam store? can you give a short yaml example, please? I don't fully understand what you're proposing yet, sorry.

I'm thinking something like:

```yaml
- name: SchedulingBasic
  template:
    - createNodes: initialNodes
    - createPods: initialPods
      podTemplatePath: config/pod-default.yaml
    - createPods: podsToMeasure
      podTemplatePath: config/pod-default.yaml
      collectMetrics: true
  workloads:
  - name: 500Nodes
    params:
      initialNodes: 500
      initialPods: 500
      podsToMeasure: 1000
```

This example is actually not compatible with the structs I proposed earlier, so they need to be adapted. The idea is that workloads (or testCases?) only define values.

Ah I see what you mean.

While this will certainly reduce verbosity, there is another approach we can take too (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93792): since nearly all tests use just one node template and one pod template, we can use have a default template for nodes and pods defined at the root of the test case and simply omit the fields inside `workloads:`.

One concern I have with your proposal is that it becomes difficult to distinguish between string values and param-mapped values for the reader. We can potentially solve that with patterns like `{{initialNodes}}` for template values that must be replaced, though. I'm not too sure about the readability of such an approach though.
casing would be another solution, something like `INITIAL_NODES`. But it's still an nit. The most important thing is making tests more flexible.

True. I think there's scope for doing both proposals: allow defining a default node/pod template *and* a workload ops template.

I like this workload templating approach; do the others have any opinions before I implement something like this?
if SkipWaitToCompletion is false, CollectMetrics is false too?

Not necessarily. The initial set of pods we schedule need to be scheduled before we can start the measurement pods, so SkipWaitToCompletion isn't set for either set of pods. However, CollectMetrics is only set for the measurement pods.
`defer collectorCancel()` in case `barrierAndCollect` fails before calling it.
Parent cancel() will take care of that? Done anyway.
there are no guarantees here that there is no `barrierAndCollect` still running at this point. Maybe we can add a wait group.
I've removed the whole async barrierAndCollect thing, so this is no longer relevant.
